title: Chope culture
fact: At some hawker centres, people reserve a seat with a tissue packet or another item. A tissue packet alone does not prove a seat is reserved.
quest: Find a different object that appears to reserve a seat. Photograph the table context; do not move anyone's belongings.
hint: Different object on a seat or table in a dining setting; not another isolated tissue packet.

title: Kopi time
fact: Local kopi orders use short codes. Kopi-O is black coffee with sugar; kopi-C uses evaporated milk and sugar. Add kosong for no sugar.
quest: Find a drinks menu displaying a kopi variation and photograph the readable name.
hint: Readable menu or sign with a kopi variant, such as kopi-O, kopi-C or kosong.

title: Kaya toast
fact: Kaya is a sweet coconut-and-egg spread. Kaya toast is commonly paired with soft-boiled eggs and kopi or teh for breakfast.
quest: Find a menu or sign explicitly naming kaya toast.
hint: Readable kaya toast name on a menu or sign; plain toast alone is insufficient.

title: Hawker culture
fact: Hawker centres bring many independently run food stalls into a shared dining space. They are everyday places to eat and gather.
quest: Photograph a stall sign showing the name of a dish you want to learn about.
hint: Readable food stall sign naming a dish.

title: Return your tray
fact: Tray-return stations help keep shared dining areas ready for the next person. Follow the signs for the appropriate return point.
quest: Find a tray-return station and photograph its sign. Keep the walkway clear.
hint: Clearly identifiable tray return station or readable tray return sign.

title: MRT manners
fact: Let passengers alight before boarding. Queue markings and station signs help everyone share the space.
quest: Find a queue marking or courtesy sign at a station. Photograph it from a safe place.
hint: Clear station queue marking or public transport courtesy sign; no need to capture faces.

title: The void deck
fact: Many HDB blocks have an open ground-floor space called a void deck. These spaces can support everyday neighbourly encounters and community activities.
quest: Find a community noticeboard or shared seating area near a housing block.
hint: Noticeboard or communal seating in housing common space; respect private information.

title: Shophouse stories
fact: Many traditional shophouses combine street-level business space with upper floors. Covered five-foot ways provide sheltered pedestrian routes.
quest: Find and photograph a covered walkway beside a row of shophouses.
hint: Covered pedestrian arcade adjacent to recognisable shophouses.

title: Pasar malam
fact: A pasar malam is a temporary night market, often with food, shopping and games. The name comes from Malay for night market.
quest: Find a sign explicitly saying pasar malam.
hint: Readable pasar malam wording; an arbitrary market is not enough.

title: Singlish spotted
fact: Expressions such as shiok and paiseh appear in informal Singapore speech. Shiok can express enjoyment; paiseh can convey embarrassment or an apology, depending on context.
quest: Find a public sign or menu containing shiok or paiseh.
hint: Readable shiok or paiseh on public signage or a menu.
